observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South is a compact head-on fish: two yellow eyes looking at the camera, a downturned mouth with hanging barbels, pectoral fins splayed out to both sides, and a narrow fan of orange-tipped comb spines rising straight up from the top of the head and back. East is a long side-profile fish in teal and cream with orange blotches. It has two runs of tall separate comb spines along the back, a forked orange-edged tail, a limb-like pectoral fin, barbels and a yellow eye. North is a narrow body seen end-on with a thin crest of comb spines rising at the top, small fins splayed at the sides and a long thin orange vertical streak trailing below the body. North shows no eyes. All three have about the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view of the fish. The face points straight at the camera: two eyes, a mouth and barbels. There are concentric orange-and-teal band markings on the forehead and flanks. observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South: a compact, roughly triangular silver body seen end-on. A round, dark-red ringed sucker mouth sits in the centre, a tall spike rises at the top, and curved fins splay out on both sides. East: a long, slender silver eel in true side profile. A round tubular sucker mouth with a pale rim is on the right, with a small eye behind it. A row of swept-back sharp fins runs along the back and a second row along the belly, and the body tapers to a whip tail on the left. North: a small, narrow, spindle-shaped silver body. Its blunt rounded end is at the top and a thin tail spike points straight down. Paired curved fins splay left and right all along it, like ribs on a fishbone. It sits noticeably lower on its canvas than the other two facings.
observed.south.png: End-on head view. Ringed sucker mouth in the centre, a dorsal spike above, and fins radiating sideways and down. Painterly grey-silver shading, thin dark edge, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side profile of a knife-slender silver eel. Fine longitudinal striations, a row of sharp fins above and below, a round rasp-ringed sucker mouth at the front, a small dark eye. Clean alpha, painterly.
observed.north.png: A small vertical spindle. Rounded top, tail spike at the bottom, about 5–6 pairs of curved fins splayed symmetrically left and right. No mouth or eye visible. It reads like a shrunken overhead view of the eel's back, with head up and tail down, rather than a foreshortened rear seen from the oblique camera.
